subject: Mutual action plan: success definitions, exit logic, and verification plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan: success definitions, exit logic, and verification plan

Samir / Leah —

Attached is a first-pass MAP for the HealthBridge pilot. At a high level we want to make the acceptance criteria unambiguous so your team and ours can move to a decision quickly. Key sections below; full matrix in the attached spreadsheet (MHP_MAP_v1.xlsx).

Core success criteria (POC / pilot scope):
- Quality: concordance on a 300-case clinical sample >= 92% (primary metric: clinical-relevance F1 on the labeled set).
- Latency: end-to-end inference p95 < 350 ms for 512-token requests under representative load (see load profile in sheet "Traffic").
- Stability: no more than 1 error-rate spike above 1% in a 24-hour window during smoke runs.
- Security/compliance: VPC peering + SOC 2 evidence review complete.

Exit gates (hard stops):
- Fail quality: if primary metric drops >= 5 percentage points vs baseline on the verification sample and fails two consecutive daily re-checks, we pause rollout and revert to previous model variant.
- SLA breach: 3 consecutive days with p95 latency exceeding target by >30% triggers an infra rollback & incident review.

Acceptance tests (what we'll run together):
1) Smoke verification (owner: HealthBridge / Leah; run window: 2 hours) — run 100 canonical queries, check concordance and failure modes.
2) Regression sweep (owner: Redwood, Ben) — 3,000-case randomized run comparing baseline -> candidate.
3) Load soak (owner: Redwood infra) — 2-hour soak at 80% expected traffic. Track p95/p99 and errors.
4) Security checklist (owner: HealthBridge security) — confirm access controls, log retention settings, KMS integration.

Owners & timeline:
- Proposed pilot window: Dec 16–Dec 21.
- Target decision date (pilot signoff): Dec 22.
- Deliverables before pilot: test-case CSV (Leah), baseline labeling report (HealthBridge / clinical SME), network access (HealthBridge infra).

Open asks for you:
1) Confirm the two-week pilot window above and whether your team needs more time for label prep.
2) Accept or propose adjustments to the core metrics (quality / latency).
3) Confirm security reviewer and point-of-contact for SOC 2 evidence.

If this looks good we can mark the attached MAP as v1 and run the smoke tests during the week of the 16th.

Thanks —

Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MHP_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP matrix, owners, test matrices)

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: success definitions, exit logic, and verification plan

Thanks Mina — really helpful framing. A few quick pieces from our side:

- We like the structure. Two small asks on the metrics: for the pilot phase we can accept a p95 latency target of 500 ms (our infra is routing through an internal proxy) and then require 350 ms for the production acceptance. Can we codify a two-tier gating (Pilot / Prod)?
- On quality: 92% concordance as a primary goal is reasonable; would you add an "acceptable drift" clause (e.g., tolerance of up to 3 points reduction during the pilot provided remediation steps are actionable)?
- Our security reviewer will be Leah Ortiz (copied). Leah will need the SOC 2 summary and network diagram by EOD Wednesday (Dec 10).

Also looping in two questions from our product team: who is owning the regression sweep dataset? We will provide 300 labeled clinical cases, but we want a Redwood-owned baseline run for comparability.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, HealthBridge
samir@healthbridge.com

Samir / Leah —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Happy to adopt a two-tier gating model — I'll sketch it out below and update the workbook:

Tier 1 — Pilot Acceptance (goal: safe signal for customer testing)
- Quality: concordance >= 89% on the pilot 300-case sample OR a documented remediation plan if 86–89%. If < 86% -> fail.
- Latency: p95 < 500 ms.
- Stability: no >= 2% sustained error rate during smoke run.

Tier 2 — Production Acceptance (post pilot, pre-prod flip)
- Quality: concordance >= 92% on a larger verification set (3,000 cases regression sweep).
- Latency: p95 < 350 ms sustained across two representative 4-hour windows.
- Security: SOC 2 summary, KMS in place, audit log routing verified.

Remediation & rollback language (suggested):
- If Pilot Acceptance passes but Prod Acceptance fails, we agree to a 2-week remediation window with defined owners and test milestones; if remediation fails or produces quality regression >5 pts vs baseline, we will revert traffic to the prior model variant and open a joint incident review.

Regression dataset ownership: Redwood (Ben) will run the baseline -> candidate sweep using the HealthBridge-provided 300-case labeled sample + an anonymized subset from our public test fixtures to reach the 3,000 cases. We'll share reproducible notebooks and the exact seed/sample used.

I'll update MHP_MAP_v1.xlsx to include the Pilot vs Prod columns and add specific owners and dates. Can everyone review the updated MAP by EOD Monday (Dec 14) so we can lock the pilot schedule?

Thanks —
Mina

Attachments: link to updated MAP (will attach v1.1 once Leah confirms SOC2 reviewer)

I'll mark ownership in the MAP and add a procurement note (PO may be required before we run sustained load). Marissa — can you take the procurement action to get a PO in if HealthBridge signs off?

Mina / team —

This reads well. Leah confirmed security review and will send SOC 2 summary by EOD tomorrow. HealthBridge accepts the MAP with the Pilot / Prod gating model described. We agree to the pilot window Dec 16–21 and target signoff Dec 22.

Two quick notes:
- We will raise the PO this week; expect procurement to complete by Dec 15 close of business.
- If the pilot produces a 3–5 point quality dip but remediation steps are actionable and progressing, HealthBridge will still move to the remediation cadence rather than certify a hard fail — consistent with the tolerance language above.

Please attach the updated MAP v1.1 when ready and confirm the final run time for regression sweep on Dec 16 (Ben) so our SMEs can be on call.

Best,
Samir
